articles.description: British and Germans themselves share stereotype but other nationalities are likelier to put out towels – or umbrellas Germans are sunlounger hoggers, or so the longstanding stereotype goes. articles.title: 'We do not want it here': CNN insiders shred MAGA billionaire's plea
articles.description: CNN insiders shredded an op-ed by a MAGA billionaire who's trying to take over their parent company, according to a media reporter. During an episode of the Status podcast Power Lines , Oliver Darcy, who reports on media, said that CNN staffers and journalists panned a New York Times op-ed by Paramount Skydance owner David Ellison , who is trying to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. Ellison controls CBS , which has seen a MAGA makeover of its news programs under Bari Weiss and cut the Trump-critical The Late Show with Stephen Colbert . The Paramount chief's guest essay marked his first public defense of the deal, which a dozen states sued to block. A judge halted it until a trial set for March, but if it's greenlit, Ellison would take control of CNN. Darcy said that he spoke with more than a dozen people inside CNN about whether the essay swayed them, and they responded with a "resounding no." "We all have eyes and ears and see what's happening at CBS," one employee told Darcy. "You can't just write an op-ed and erase that." Another called out Weiss, whose leadership has seen the gutting of ' 60 Minutes ' and the ratings of CBS Mornings and CBS Evening News plummet . "The thing David Ellison seems to be missing is the wild mismanagement and disrespect that Bari has displayed at 60 and CBS," the CNN staffer told Darcy. "We see it, and we do not want it here." A third CNN staffer told Darcy that the changes Ellison directed at CBS News "eroded the newsroom's trust," and concluded, "Free pressifying CNN is not the answer." In the op-ed, Ellison wrote that he does not wish to bend newsrooms to his views, and said he wants them to reflect "the whole world, not one side of it." Darcy read that line as signaling which side Ellison believes is underrepresented. "I don't think he believes that liberals are underrepresented," Darcy said. "I think he believes that conservatives are underrepresented in media." Darcy also noted that Paramount didn't respond to his request for comment.

articles.title: Loyal Republicans live in terror of being 'murdered' for crossing Trump: ex-GOP operative
articles.description: The MAGA movement has grown so menacing that even loyal Republicans now fear for their lives, veteran GOP strategist Rick Wilson said this week. Speaking with Wajahat Ali on the "Left Hook" podcast — the same conversation in which he predicted a Republican midterm blowout — the Lincoln Project co-founder recounted what happened to a former client, a member of Congress who backed Jeb Bush, then Ted Cruz, before endorsing Donald Trump late in the 2016 primary. He was no radical, Wilson said. The trouble started at the lawmaker's first town hall after Trump's inauguration. A man in a red hat demanded to know whether the congressman would vote with Trump 100 percent of the time. When the lawmaker said he would put his district first, "his wife had received 10 death threats about their children," Wilson said. Wilson argued the overwhelming share of political intimidation now comes from one direction, estimating that 99 percent of the threats, doxxing and swatting he sees originate on the right. Everyone who has pulled a gun on him or pounded on his door over the past decade, he claimed, has been MAGA. Across a 35-year career, he counted exactly one death threat from a Democratic-leaning person — a man who turned out to be severely mentally ill. Now, he said, he gets one every day or two. "You can be murdered if you oppose Trump. That's okay with the MAGA base," Wilson said, describing Republican officeholders as living in terror of the president. Wilson tied the menace to a party fracturing in once-solid red states , with Trump himself now facing what could sink the GOP this fall.

articles.title: Republicans 'absolutely apoplectic' as Trump put them in 'impossible situation': reporter
articles.description: Republicans are "tearing their hair out" as President Donald Trump stomps on the midterm messaging, a New York Times journalist said. During an appearance on CNN, Lulu Garcia-Navarro spoke about the GOP's frustrations as Trump blames them for voters' anger ahead of the midterm while praising himself. "They are tearing their hair out. They are absolutely apoplectic," Garcia-Navarro said. "They have tried to get President Trump on message." During an interview with Punchbowl News' Jake Sherman, Trump said that voters are "not angry at me," but "they are angry at Republicans." On CNN, former Fox News anchor Gretchen Carlson noted that Trump wouldn't admit to being down in the polls or unpopular with voters, and "he's going to blame it on Republicans," adding, "Rest assured, if the midterms are bad for Republicans, he will say it was because he was not on the ballot." Garcia-Navarro agreed, adding that Republicans have "tried to get President Trump on message" ahead of the midterms. "He has completely stepped on that message over and over again," Garcia-Navarro said. "He's also made it impossible for them to separate from him because they actually do need his base to show up for them," she said. "But then they can't actually go out and try and attract new voters because he's like a lodestone around their necks." Republicans' dependence on a president they can't get on message puts them "in an impossible situation," Garcia-Navarro said. "As you look at the midterms, it's really hard for Republicans." Garcia-Navarro said "the only saving grace" for Republicans is attacking faults in the Democratic Party platform and a boost from redistricting. "Ultimately, it's going to have to be not just a blue wave, but a blue tidal wave in order to sort of get past some of these structural things," Garcia-Navarro said.

articles.title: MAGA battered by epic clapback over surging Dem's supposed 'hot mic' moment
articles.description: Republican activists are running wild with a recently resurfaced quote from Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed — but he's hitting back over it. El-Sayed, an Egyptian-American public health administrator and progressive activist nominated after a monthslong hard-fought primary, offhandedly commented during the 2020 documentary How To Fix A Primary, "I hate Mackinac so much. Every time I've ever come here, I've hated it. Why am I here?" while on a campaign stop at the famous Michigan tourist destination. This triggered a MAGA meltdown, with far-right account End Wokeness taking to X to trash the Democratic nominee. "Abdul El-Sayed hot mic: 'I hate Mackinac so much,'" wrote the account, including a video of the picturesque countryside on the island. "This is the most American place in MI." El-Sayed noticed the jab and went online to punch back. "Not sure about 'End Wokeness,' but I don’t think the most 'American place in MI' can be a place that ... bans cars," wrote El-Sayed, referencing the state's huge dependence on the auto industry. El-Sayed is running for the seat being vacated by current Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. His Republican opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers, has lost no time in firing up a campaign laden with Islamophobic dog whistles .

articles.title: Trump's newest blame-game play enrages: 'District isn’t Trump’s personal property!'
articles.description: The Trump administration — fresh off a failed attempt to blame vandals for botched work on the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — has tried once again to dodge responsibility and enraged locals in the process. Trump's latest political jab spurred one D.C. local to snap off a photo and send it to Newsweek , along with a vent over her frustration. The photo shows that the National Park Service has posted a sign on the monument blaming previous administrations for neglecting the site, claiming "more than half of the 58 water supply ports were so clogged that they were deemed nonfunctioning." The sign read: "The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has been partially refilled to allow National Park Service staff and contractors to flush the pool's piping system for the first time in more than a decade." It also told the public that the flushing process could "temporarily discolor the water as buildup in the pipes is cleaned out." Suzanne Garwood told Newsweek she was livid. "They just took down the extended fencing from the Fourth so this is the first time we could get that close to the pool in weeks," Garwood fumed. "The East Wing, the Kennedy Center, the Arts of War and Peace, and the Pool. Next up is the Arch and destroying our cherry trees for a golf course. The District isn’t Trump’s personal property."
